In this study, we propose a resource allocation framework that leverages the transparency and immutability of blockchain to enhance data integrity and security in IoT applications. The blockchain-based method is utilized to identify the malicious users in the IoT applications. The proposed method is implemented in MATLAB and performance is evaluated by performance metrics such as the probability of detection, false alarm probability, average network throughput, and energy efficiency. The proposed method is compared by existing methods such as Friend or Foe and Tidal Trust Algorithm. To further optimize this process, we introduce a Hybrid Artificial Bee Colony-Whale Optimization Algorithm (ABC-WOA), a powerful optimization technique designed to minimize time delays and energy consumption in IoT environments. Our findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in achieving resource efficiency, reducing time and conserving energy within IoT networks.

articleTitle: Lung Cancer Stage Classification Utilizing k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN)
abstract: The classification of stages is a well-established practice encompassing both biological sciences and engineering domains. This procedure involves a clinical evaluation of the disease's advancement and distribution. Given the considerable global impact of lung cancer on mortality rates, achieving precise early detection and accurate stage classification holds utmost importance for effective therapeutic interventions. This research introduces an inventive strategy to bolster the existing lung cancer stage classification framework. It accomplishes this by integrating Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and the k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) method. The primary objective is twofold: to precisely ascertain the presence of lung cancer cells and to determine the corresponding stages through the analysis of CT-scan images. By synergizing the k-NN and CNN methodologies, the study aspires to realize an elevated level of result accuracy. This holistic approach exhibits the potential to revolutionize lung cancer diagnosis and consequently enhance overall patient well-being.

articleTitle: The Grid-Based Service Discovery in Mobile Ad Hoc Networks
abstract: It is anticipated that Service Discovery would play a vital role in the future of mobile ad hoc networks (MANETs). There are already a variety of service discovery procedures, but many of them are designed for use with wired networks or short-range, ad hoc wireless connections with just one hop. In this research, we offer a new method for discovering services in MANET based on hierarchical grid designs. MANET uses a 2D logical hierarchical grid to divide up the world. We choose a directory node for each grid to store the descriptions of vendors' services that have been recorded in order to respond to requests from users. We suggest service registrations as well as discover propagation strategies to improve the performance of these processes. Grids of registering patterns are used to record the details of the sharing service. When an applicant has a need for a service, it follows the search path to learn more about what's available. Finally, the results prove that our approach is effective over a wide range of connections densities as well as sizes.

articleTitle: Methods of Identifying and Reducing Covert Channel Attacks: An Analysis
abstract: Many people have long been interested in secret interaction across a system of connections. It has drawn not just trustworthy entities to interact covertly with one another, but also attackers/ hackers to develop methods to uncover as well as disclose data and utilize the system in manners that break safety protocols. Covert channels have been employed to transport data in a secure manner. Encryption just prevents interaction from being decrypted by unauthorized entities, while covert channels seek to conceal the interaction's actual presence. These kinds of channels first came to light as a threat to safety on monolithic structures like mainframe computing systems. In recent years, the focus of protocols of the computer networks has switched to hidden channel routes. The web's massive volume of information as well as wide variety of diverse protocols make it an excellent raised bandwidth medium for secret interactions. This survey shows the overview of the mechanisms adopted for the detection and the mitigation of the covert channel-specific attacks that might ruin the confidentiality of the data being transmitted from one source to the other destination. Finally, the concluding remarks along with the future possibilities of the covert channel attacks are indicated.

articleTitle: Empowering Rural Minds: Leveraging Predictive Analytics to Bridge Urban-Rural Educational Disparities Through Financial Assistance
abstract: Access to quality education is a critical factor in individual empowerment, economic development, and societal progress. However, students from rural backgrounds often face significant obstacles when it comes to pursuing technical education, primarily due to financial barriers. Financial barriers act as a deterrent, restricting the participation of rural students in technical education programmes. This paper presents an innovative approach to address this issue by leveraging the power of artificial intelligence (AI) and predictive analytics to provide equitable financial assistance and scholarships for technical education. By adopting a comprehensive strategy, this paper addresses the biases, transparency shortcomings, and contextual factors that have been prevalent in previous algorithm methods. The strategy employed in this study involves a multi-faceted approach, integrating various methodologies to achieve optimal outcomes. The key steps encompassed in the methodology include algorithmic fairness, model training and selection, transparency and interpretability, human-in-the-loop review, contextualised assessment, continuous learning, and feedback loops. Adversarial Debiasing is utilised to mitigate biases and ensure a fair decision-making process. To enhance transparency and interpretability, rule-based systems and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations) are employed. Human-in-the-loop review is an integral part of the methodology, ensuring that AI-driven decisions are validated and refined by human experts. The expected outcome of this research is an AI-enabled financial assistance system that democratises technical education by making it more accessible to students from rural backgrounds. The implementation of this model can have a transformative impact on education equality, empowering rural minds to pursue their academic dreams.

articleTitle: Enhancing Crop Yields with Smart Agriculture Systems using Solar Trackers
abstract: Smart irrigation systems have become an important tool in modern agriculture to improve crop yields and conserve water resources. However, these systems often rely on electricity, which can be expensive and unreliable in remote or rural areas. To address this issue, this research paper proposes the use of a solar tracking system to maximize the efficiency of smart irrigation systems. The research paper presents the design and implementation of a smart irrigation system with a solar tracking system in a greenhouse environment. The system was tested using different irrigation strategies and solar panel orientations to determine the optimal configuration for maximizing efficiency. It demonstrates the potential of using a solar tracking system to maximize the efficiency of smart irrigation systems. The proposed system can be easily replicated and scaled up for use in different agricultural settings, providing an eco-friendly and costeffective solution for irrigation management.

articleTitle: ADMM: Computational Analysis of Lasso and Ridge on Fraud Detection
abstract: Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers or ADMM is becoming increasingly vital in resolving regression and classification problems with complex datasets containing a variety of attributes or features. As datasets grow in complexity, ADMM's ability to efficiently handle large-scale optimization problems becomes crucial for achieving accurate and effective solutions in regression and classification tasks. Its versatility makes it well-suited for addressing the challenges posed by intricate datasets, ensuring optimal performance in various domains such as machine learning, signal processing, and image analysis. This paper compares the implementation of both LASSO and Ridge regression techniques using ADMM with the traditional non-distributed single-machine implementation of both techniques. Through simulations, the significantly reduced computational time achieved by the regression models optimised by ADMM is highlighted compared to the standard regression approaches.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: TrustDroid: Enhancing Trust and Privacy for Android Mobile Phones by Preventing Riskware and SMS Malware
abstract: Android mobile phones are widely targeted by SMS Malware and Riskware attacks for stealing users' private information like user credentials, pictures, videos, banking credentials etc. Android users are not aware of the incoming link or message and unintentionally allow attackers to intrude on their mobile devices. The objective of this research paper is to enhance user confidence and privacy on Android smartphones. The CICMalDroid 2020 dataset provides the foundation for this research work by having a dataset on traffic patterns of riskware and SMS malware attacks on Android smartphones. In this research work, the methodology is proposed for early detection of riskware and SMS malware attacks by integrating a machine learning-trained chip at the hardware level. The dataset is trained with multiple machine learning algorithms to explore the effectiveness of appropriate algorithms for devising solutions for the detection of Android malware attacks. The results prove the efficiency of the random forest technique for the CICMalDroid dataset. This classifier has the best accuracy, recall, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F1$</tex> score in comparison with other classifiers on the taken dataset. The Naive Bayes approach, on the other hand, is dependable and reduces the incidence of false positives. These results not only highlight the need to reinforce cybersecurity and regularly update software, but they also highlight the importance of machine learning in terms of Android device security.

articleTitle: Multiclass Classification of Malware using Machine Learning
abstract: This work aims to classify malware into one of its nine families using multiclass classification using machine learning. Due to the rising number of malware assaults on numerous devices, including workstations, servers, cloud instances, and mobile devices, endpoint security is a critical concern for organizations today. Finding and stopping malware activity has become crucial to guaranteeing data security, privacy, and protection to defend against such attacks. It is even more critical to take safeguards now because of the wide variety of virus activities occurring across online and offline files. Using machine learning algorithms to forecast malware effectively by using malware detection datasets is one of the most efficient approaches to deal with this problem. Large amounts of data may be analysed by machine learning algorithms, which can also spot patterns that humans might find difficult to see. These methods enable more precise malware prediction and detection, which is crucial for endpoint security. Given that it is an affordable and effective option for endpoint security, the use of machine learning algorithms in malware detection is growing in popularity. Therefore, this work aims to employ three machine learning algorithms for analysing and classifying the malware present in a dataset. The dataset used in this work is the Microsoft BIG dataset which contains malware files belonging to nine different families. The malware files are converted to a feature dataset using feature selection and normalization techniques. This feature dataset is then exposed to classification algorithms like Random Forest, LightGBM and XGBoost which are known for their performance. Each model is assessed on the log loss of overall prediction. In this work, XGBoost showed the lowest log loss with value 0.046699789818985364.

articleTitle: The Scheme for Recharging Nodes in Surveillance Wireless Sensor Networks Using Dynamic Resource Location
abstract: Sensor nodes in wireless sensor networks are dispersed at random and are used to keep tabs on whatever is of interest. Due to the restricted battery capacity of each sensor, it might be difficult to keep the network running for continuous observation. Using a mobile charger to recharge the sensor wirelessly is becoming a viable option for powering the sensors. However, because to uncertainty in the networks, choosing an effective charging route for the MC is difficult. Due to unpredictability in the network architecture, such as node failures, the pace at which the sensors use energy may vary dramatically. Because of these modifications, the relative significance of the various sensors, often treated as equivalent in previous publications, varies. We suggest a novel adaptive pricing mechanism in this study, one that makes use of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to address these problems. In specifically, the MC uses a charging technique that decides which sensor should be charged next depending on the overall network's health. We then use a deep neural network, taught with RL techniques, to determine appropriate values for the price variables. Our model is flexible enough to accommodate changes in the architecture of a network. Results show that the proposed method greatly outperforms the best existing ondemand alternatives.

articleTitle: A Novel AC-DC Hybrid Microgrid Architecture Based on Modular Multilevel and Its Control Strategy
abstract: In order to adapt to the large-scale distributed renewable energy microgrid system, this paper designs a new type of microgrid architecture based on the modular multilevel converter (MMC) as the AC/DC hybrid microgrid interconnecting converter, which can absorb more new energy sources and further improve the power quality of the system. First, the DC microgrid structure and control strategy composed of distributed power sources, and the AC microgrid structure and control strategy under large-scale photovoltaic power generation system are analyzed in detail. The mathematical model of MMC interconnect converter is established, and a common control strategy between DC side and AC side is proposed to stabilize the DC bus voltage and AC bus voltage. Virtual synchronous machine technology is introduced to enable the converter to achieve power synchronization control and provide virtual inertia support for the microgrid. Finally, a simulation model of the microgrid is established by Matlab/Simulink computer simulation platform, and different working conditions are simulated and verified, and the simulation results show the correctness and validity of the proposed microgrid architecture and strategy.

articleTitle: Automated Diabetic Retinopathy Prediction Using a Deep Learning Based Modified DenseNet
abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a form of diabetes caused by damage to the retinal blood vessels. Early identification and treatment of this condition are facilitated through retinal screening. DR progresses through five phases: usual, malignant, acute, moderate and slight. To enable early detection and intervention, computer-aided diagnostic methods are essential. Numerous deep learning-based automated approaches have demonstrated their effectiveness in accurately grading DR. In this paper, a deep leaning technique called modified Densenet-169 is proposed for early detection of DR. Initially, the retinal images are pre-processed using Gabor filter to enhance the visibility of blood vessels for easy detection of DR. Then the size of the dataset is increased by using image data generator. Finally, the images are processed in modified Densenet-169 which classifies retinal images as absence of DR, light DR, beginner DR, serious DR, and progressive DR. The performance of DenseNet is enhanced by including four pairs of dense blocks and transition layers. Dense block in DenseNet combines feature maps by concatenation, while the transition layer reduces the dimensions via a composite of average pooling, 1x1 convolution, and batch normalization. The empirical observations showcase that the modified Densenet169, as proposed, achieves superior levels of accuracy, precision, and recall in DR detection than cutting-edge methods.

articleTitle: Deep Q-Network-based Stock Market Optimization for improving Stock Trends
abstract: The emergence of new technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, and the Internet of Things (IoT) has left a significant impact on several aspects of our lives. These technologies have found their way into various financial domains, including stock markets, banking, and insurance. In this paper, we propose an intelligent system for the stock market that is based on deep Q-learning and aims to enhance its performance. Our proposed system evaluates the stock market by analyzing past and current actions and predicting their outcomes. Based on the evaluation results, the system provides efficient rewards. To estimate the suitable actions and enhance its learning process, the state information is fed into a convolutional neural network (CNN), which estimates the ‘Q-values.’ Our system uses a deep Q-learning algorithm, a type of reinforcement learning that systematically improves the agent's performance by learning from its experience. The results show that our proposed scheme for predicting the stock market outperforms conventional methods. With an accuracy rate of 89%, the proposed system is a highly effective tool for predicting market trends with increased efficiency. The system is capable of analyzing complex patterns and making informed decisions based on past and current market trends. With the help of this intelligent system, investors can make better decisions, reduce risks, and improve the overall performance of the stock market.

articleTitle: Face Recognition Application in Flutter
abstract: This research paper explores the integration of Google's FaceNet model with the Flutter framework to create a highly accurate and efficient facial recognition system. The paper discusses the architecture of FaceNet, emphasizing its ability to extract facial features and perform accurate facial matching. The challenges and considerations involved in integrating a deep learning model into Flutter are addressed, focusing on optimization techniques and resource management. The proposed integration holds promise for secure authentication systems, personalized user experiences, and augmented reality applications. Performance evaluations and experiments validate the effectiveness of the integrated model, providing valuable insights for developers and researchers interested in leveraging facial recognition technology within the Flutter ecosystem. The integration of FaceNet with Flutter makes room for new possibilities in advanced mobile applications, bridging the gap between deep learning and cross-platform development.

articleTitle: An Uncertainty-Aware Transfer Learning-Based Framework for COVID-19v Diagnosis
abstract: More and more studies are looking at the use of dynamic off-chain transportation in IoT systems that are based on payment channel networks (PCNs). Flexible routing in PCN-based IoT, where devices often have little resources, has two key challenges, however. The primary problem is figuring out how to make PCNs with variable channel capacity work efficiently for long-term transactions. The second issue is how to maximise transaction efficiency (the number of successful payments and the proportion of those that go through) by employing a lightweight routing strategy on IoT gadgets. To achieve this objective, we propose a powerful deep reinforcement training method for learning the combined flexible and lightweight routing approach. We use a proximal policy optimising strategy to attain the best effectiveness in dynamic routing problems for off-chain systems via an actorcritic learning structure to train the instructor's DRL model. By using an adaptive pruning strategy to remove superfluous network parameters from the teacher model without compromising the latter's receptiveness to new information, we are able to generate a compact and effective DRL model for the student. The effectiveness of the pupil's network is also improved by the use of knowledge distillation. Therefore, it may be possible to construct a small and efficient pupil DRL model and utilise it to optimise the long-term efficacy of operations in off-chain networks on limited-resource IoT devices. Results from computer simulations show that the suggested DRL algorithm improves PCN transaction performance compared to the baseline techniques, while using just <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10{{\% }}$</tex> of the resources available in the original instructor model.

articleTitle: The Architecture for End-to-End 5G Network Slice Resource Management and Orchestration
abstract: A new paradigm is developing in 5G networks in which cloud environments are used to do calculations for different mobile apps. A general computing platform may be realized with the help of compute, storage, as well as networking resources made available by both edge and core clouds. Many services, especially those that are latencysensitive or computationally intensive, might benefit from network slicing techniques in a shared-resource setting. This study recommends a method of resource management for providing the highest possible Quality of Experience (QoE) to users in terms of delayed gap tolerance. The Min-Fit approach is an example of an answer based on heuristics; it finds a server having the most CPU power and places it in charge of meeting customers' demands. A mathematical model for 5G slicing capability is created to optimize the delay gap through resource management and enhance user experience. Several computational experiments serving as performance evaluations demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed strategy for slicing. The results show that our approach is more effective than other algorithms that take more time to complete their tasks.

articleTitle: Image Forgery Detection using ELA and CNN
abstract: Picture tampering has recently increased due to the increasing popularity of photo-editing software, making it difficult to determine the authenticity of an image with the naked eye. To address this issue, we proposed a model that detects image forgeries using ELA (Error Level Analysis) and CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) techniques. ELA is a forensic tool that examines variations in compression levels, whereas CNN is a deep learning technique that can learn and extract features from photos to categorize them as either modified or legitimate. The model combines both techniques and was tested on the publicly available CASIA 2.0 dataset. According to the results, the proposed model outperforms existing deep learning models in terms of training time and computational efficiency, achieving an overall accuracy of more than 95.19%. The proposed method is an effective and efficient method for detecting a wide range of image editing techniques used for image manipulation.

articleTitle: A Transfer Learning-Based Framework Aware of Uncertainty for Diagnosing COVID-19
abstract: Preventing and controlling an epidemic of COVID-19 requires rapid and accurate patient detection. There are real issues concerning the reliability and efficacy of the PCR tests used to identify COVID-19, and many of these assays are not accessible in many countries. In light of these constraints, this study introduces a transfer learning approach that takes uncertainty into account while searching for COVID-19 in medical images. ResNet50, VGGI6, DenseNetl21, as well as InceptionResNetV2 are four popular convolution neural networks (CNNs) used to extract deep attributes from chest X-ray and CT scans. To identify COVID 19, the collected attributes are fed into several machine learning and statistical modeling frameworks. In addition, we compute and make available the conceptual uncertainty of classification findings, which may be used to spot situations in which trained models are unsure of their verdicts (out-of-distribution issue). Sensitivity, precision, sensitivity, and ROC-curve area-under-the-curve are all maximised using linear support vector machines along with neural network models for huge simulated X-ray as well as CT scan data sets. It is also shown that the uncertainty in CT image predictions is much higher than in X-ray image predictions.

articleTitle: Automatic Approach Based on Deep Learning for Tea Leaf Disease Detection
abstract: Tea production is an essential agricultural business, but it is vulnerable to various illnesses that can reduce productivity and quality. This study uses Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to provide a unique technique for automated categorization of tea leaf illnesses. An extensive collection of 900 high-resolution pictures illustrating eight different types of leaf spot (Red leaf spot, Algal leaf spot, Bird's eyespot, grey blight, White spot, Anthracnose, and Brown spot). Tea leaf diseases (blight.) were curated. A cutting-edge CNN model architecture was created and trained to utilize a deep learning framework and obtained 84.5% classification accuracy. The model has standard criteria such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score were used to assess performance. The outcomes are essential for the tea business since the automated disease classification system can give realtime illness categorization. Tea estates can be monitored in real-time for early disease identification and intervention. This may result in increased tea production, improved crop management, and decreased economic losses for tea producers.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning for Early Tomato Leaf Disease Detection: A CNN Approach
abstract: This article introduces automated tomato leaf disease detection using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). The work trains a CNN-based model to reliably distinguish healthy and sick tomato leaves using 2,000 photos. The model's capacity to recognize modest visual cues from diverse illnesses suggests it might be a viable early disease detection tool. The experimental findings show 96 % accuracy on the test dataset. CNN disease identification is a major step towards sustainable crop management. The model's ability to speed up disease diagnosis, intervene when needed, and reduce crop losses suggests it might boost crop yields and agricultural resilience. These results apply to many agricultural fields outside tomato growing. In conclusion, deep learning in agriculture may bridge the gap between traditional practices and technology innovation, increasing crop productivity and agricultural system resilience. This research promotes a future where technology and sustainable agriculture work together to develop precision agriculture.

articleTitle: Predictive Maintenance: A Comprehensive Analysis and Future Outlook
abstract: Predictive maintenance (PdM), a maintenance strategy that uses data analytics and cutting-edge technology to predict equipment failures before they occur. The paper explains how PdM works, the importance of sensors, and the tools that form the backbone of PdM. The paper also explores the limitations of PdM and the importance of reliability- centered maintenance (RCM). The advantages of PdM include reducing downtime, reducing operating costs, and optimizing efficiency. However, the paper also highlights the challenges of PdM, such as concerns about data quality, the need for initial investment, and the need to train skilled workers. Looking ahead, the paper discusses how PdM will blend with Industry 4.0, bringing forth a manufacturing revolution through factories and digital twin technology. The paper concludes that PdM will extend its influence to sectors like healthcare, transportation, and energy, guaranteeing the dependability of vital systems in these domains.

articleTitle: Enhancing Deep Neural Networks through Pruning followed by Quantization Pipeline: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: In numerous applications, deep neural networks have proven to have outstanding skills. Complex network architectures, on the other hand, provide difficulties for effective real-time deployment and demand a substantial amount of computational resources and energy. Network compression is one example of an optimization that can be used to address these issues. Network compression can often be implemented with minimal loss of accuracy. In certain cases, accuracy may even increase. Two types of network compression are reviewed in this study: quantization and pruning. We contrast pruning methods and discuss the standards used to weed out unnecessary computations. Quantization decreases computations by lowering the datatype's precision. Although systems with a smaller bit width, like binary neural networks, are also taken into consideration, weights, biases, and activations may often be quantized to 8-bit integers. You can use quantization and trimming alone or together. We in this paper discuss contrast existing approaches of quantization, pruning and hybrid optimization. Give findings of compressed network accuracy on various frameworks using hybrid optimization technique.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Intelligent Power Quality Event Recognition Through MRA-DWT in Combination with AdaBoost Classifier
abstract: The reliable and efficient operation of electrical power systems is paramount in modern society, necessitating the continuous monitoring and timely recognition of power quality disturbances. This paper presents an intelligent approach for Power Quality Event Recognition (PQER) by combining Multiresolution Analysis with Discrete Wavelet Transform (MRA-DWT) and the AdaBoost classifier. The MRA-DWT technique allows for the decomposition of power signals into multiple scales, enabling the extraction of informative features from both time and frequency domains. Subsequently, the AdaBoost classifier is employed to enhance the classification accuracy by training an ensemble of weak learners, thereby creating a robust and adaptive PQER system. The proposed methodology is evaluated on a real-world dataset of power quality disturbances, showcasing its effectiveness in distinguishing and classifying various types of disturbances, including voltage sags, swells, interruptions, harmonics, and transients. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the MRA-DWT-AdaBoost combination over traditional methods, achieving higher accuracy and faster recognition of power quality events. This research contributes to the advancement of intelligent power quality monitoring systems, offering a promising solution for enhancing the reliability and stability of electrical grids through the timely identification and classification of power quality disturbances.

articleTitle: Bidirectional English-Marathi Translation using Pretrained Models: A Comparative Study of Different Pre-Trained Models
abstract: This study investigates the use of pre-trained models for English-to-Marathi translation. The purpose of this study is to investigate English-to-Marathi translation utilising pre-trained multilingual language models. The research examines multiple translation models accessible in the Hugging Face library, such as mbart-large-50-many-to-many-mmt, IndicBART, m2m100_1.2B, Helsinki-NLP/opus-mt-mr-en, and umtS-base. BLEU score, pre-cision, brevity penalty, ChrF score, TER score, Google Blue and Rouge are among the assessment criteria used. Because of this, we now have a bidirectional translation model, which is formed by the integration of two unidirectional models-one that translates English to Marathi and the other that translates Marathi to English. In spite of the inherent difficulties posed by language asymmetry and the limited parallel data available in bidirectional models, the purpose of this study is to investigate potential solutions to these roadblocks. According to the findings, the performance of the optimized MBART model has significantly improved, whilst the performance of the Helsinki-NLP model has essentially stayed the same. Notably, making use of MBART's setup and weight transfer led to significant improvements being made to the AI4Bharat model.

articleTitle: Sentimental Analysis of Social Media Data for Mental Health Monitoring
abstract: The mental health problem known as depression is a multifaceted and widespread condition that presents a substantial obstacle to global health. Early detection and management are critical to lessen its negative impact on people's well-being. With the rise of social media platforms like Twitter, researchers have become interested in mining their textual content for indicators of depression using deep learning techniques. This paper presents a complete methodology for detecting depression using deep learning models trained on an open-source Kaggle dataset. The proposed method employs the Transformers, i.e., BERT, to retrieve embeddings from the text data (tweets). The embeddings derived from BERT are subsequently utilized as input for the customized Deep Neural Network, which consists of five layers and an LSTM model. The experimental results show that the Deep Neural Network outpaces the LSTM model by achieving 100% and 99.13% training and validation accuracies, respectively. The utilization of deep learning methodologies to detect depression through analysis of tweets demonstrates a potentially advantageous and groundbreaking strategy for tackling the difficulties connected with diagnosing and providing assistance to those who may be undergoing depressive episodes.

articleTitle: Textual Analysis of Privacy Policies to Understand the Effect of GDPR
abstract: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) has far-reaching implications that extend beyond the European Union (EU) borders. Its visionary concepts have worked as a catalyst, inspiring states and regions worldwide to rethink their data privacy policies. The GDPR is the foundation of an international privacy framework that crosses political and cultural boundaries, encouraging a collaborative effort to protect personal data. This study aims to explore the GDPR's multifaceted effects on data privacy, including organisational, legal, and technological aspects. To provide comprehensive insights, data was collected from the privacy policies of the top 50 websites for both the pre-GDPR and postGDPR eras. Textual analysis of these policies allowed for a comparison using keyword frequency, personal information disclosure, GDPR-related terms, and the enumeration of user rights being evaluated. To examine the structural changes in privacy rules, we use the average frequency with which a specific group of words. The finding reveals that the average word count of privacy rules has increased significantly, rising from 2355.74 to 5882.82. This shift indicates a positive trend towards increasing transparency and clarity in communicating privacy policies. Privacy policies are now written in more precise, accessible language, emphasising the essence of GDPR's objective and improving user comprehension. In the post-GDPR, key terms such as “Consent,” “Data Breach,” “Data Subject,” “Data Controller,” and “Data Protection” feature prominently, indicating more awareness and more substantial compliance obligations. Implementing GDPR user rights under amended rules demonstrates a noteworthy dedication to user data protection.

articleTitle: Seven Sisters Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This research proposes a new swarm-based meta-heuristic algorithm named Seven Sisters Optimizer (SSO) in-spired by the Jungle Babbler bird flock (commonly known as Seven sisters or Seven Brothers (in Hindi)). Jungle Babbler's calls are structurally and functionally organized to serve as a coherent communication system. They have 15 different types of communication classified as affiliative (friendly), with seven call types, and agonistic (unfriendly), with eight call types. The flock head, the sentinel bird, is tasked with the keep tab on optimal habitat and orients the flock members as affiliative and agonistic. The proposed algorithm is tested on 13 well-known benchmark functions. The results of the proposed SSO are verified by a comparative study of of SSO with nine other existing optimization algorithms, which include the most widely used meta-heuristics, Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) as well as Gravitational Search Algorithm (GSA), Flower Polli-nation Algorithm (FPA), Moth-Flame Optimization (MFO), Bat Algorithm (BOA), Firefly Algorithm (FA), Cuckoo Search Algorithm (CS) along with high-performance optimizer LSHADE-SPACMA (LSP). To evaluate the constraint handling capacity of the proposed algorithm ie SSO, it is further tested on a gear design problem, and the results are compared with different classical and swarm-based optimization approaches. The results demonstrate that the proposed SSO exploration and exploitation capabilities are superior as compared to the other optimizers.

articleTitle: Role of Hardware in the Loop Testing in Model Based Design
abstract: Model based design (MBD) is a systems engineering approach for collaborative design, analysis, simulation and testing of complex systems such as embedded architectures. Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) is an important aspect of MBD wherein the functionality of the designed embedded system architecture model is tested on actual hardware for realistic performance assessments. HIL is a continuously evolving technological frame-work that is widely used in auto embedded components being made using MBD methodology. HIL has a wide range of applications in design validation, control prototyping, functional testing of integrated components, response validation under simulated conditions and more. HIL eliminates the need for costly, time intensive and sometimes safety-critical testing of embedded algorithms in actual scenarios. HIL is being preferred more and more over the traditional hardware testing methodologies as it provides a competitive edge in developing dependable and reliable auto embedded hardware systems. This paper presents a brief literature review and introduction of the hardware in the loop concept within the framework of model based design from an embedded systems perspective. HIL helps to reduce the overall development costs as well as the time to market of modern automobile industry.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Blood Cell Disease Classification: A CNN-Enhanced Approach for Accurate Hematological Diagnosis and Treatment
abstract: White blood cells, also known as leukocytes, hold significant importance within the human body as they constitute a vital component of the human immune system. The blood cells possess crucial diagnostic information for numerous diseases and play a vital role in safeguarding the body. Diseases such as leukemia, autoimmune diseases, immunological deficiencies, and hematologic disorders can be detected by evaluating the quantity of white blood cells. In contemporary times, the blood analysis process conducted by medical professionals has been associated with the potential drawbacks of time inefficiency and human immune system errors. A diagnostic system with assistance capabilities can be developed to mitigate these errors, facilitate expedited diagnosis, and alleviate the burden of effort. This study aimed to classify 12,500 white blood cell images, including four distinct white blood cell types: Eosinophil, Lymphocyte, Monocyte, and Neutrophil. A CNN model has been proposed in this research to classify the blood cells. The model has shown a very good accuracy of 96.71% and training accuracy of 98.64% with a minimal loss of 0.22. The overall average precision for all these four classes is 95%. This research can be utilized in the medical field for early diagnosis of any hematological disorder.

articleTitle: The Multicast Techniques that are Efficient for Multichannel Wireless Mesh Networks
abstract: Wireless mesh networks (WMNs) have received a lot of interest in recent years due to the realization that multicast may significantly improve their performance. However, in order to minimize overall network disturbance and increase network performance, multicast interaction in WMNs needs an effectual channel task mechanism. In order to quantify interference and address the hidden channel issue in multicast communication, the idea of local multiplex is developed in this study. Based on this idea, we offer a channel assignment technique that takes Deep Convolutional Neural Networks, or DCNN interference into account. The approach maximizes network performance by considering overlapping and non-overlapping channels. The suggested approach has been shown to enhance WMN network capacity and decrease interference in simulations.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Handwritten Descriptive Responses Using Machine Learning - A Survey
abstract: Evaluation of student performances is crucial to the process of learning in an education system. Currently, the most common approach adopted throughout the education industry is largely reliant on human resources as forms of evaluators. As the gap in student-teacher ratios increases, this process becomes complicated and cumbersome and such manual assessment techniques lead to unintentional biases and inconsistency. Technology has been playing a role in aiding evaluators in the recent trends. Instead of the traditional pen and paper-based methods, modes of assessments are being digitized and so are the correction processes. While there are several successful technologies available for grading multiple-choice questions, there is still growing research for methods of evaluating descriptive questions which need to account for a degree of variations in student answers. For the last few decades, there have been many researchers working on developing a system that would act as a bridge between traditional methods and digitized evaluation systems, by using techniques like Optical Character Recognition (OCR). Various Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniques have been proposed to evaluate descriptive answers automatically. This paper provides a comprehensive survey of such systems and analyses the drawbacks of the current studies. It has been observed that these systems do not consider essay-type questions that do not have a defined answer.

articleTitle: IoT-driven Carbon Footprint Reduction in Higher Educational Institutions
abstract: Promoting environmental responsibility and sustainable practices in educational institutions, especially colleges and universities, is crucial in the battle against climate change. Notably, carbon emissions assessments often underestimate the substantial impact of power consumption within university facilities. This paper focuses on understanding our campus's per capita carbon footprint by developing and implementing an Internet of Things (IoT) enabled smart device with energy monitoring capabilities. This device will enable us to capture real-time energy consumption data, which in turn facilitates the identification of peak usage periods and areas with heightened energy demand. Subsequently, we convert this energy consumption data into a per capita carbon footprint. This paper discusses the system architecture of the proposed IoT-enabled smart device. We selected a prominent research building within the university campus for our initial pilot study. The research building consists of three office floors and accommodates over 200 employees. Here, we deployed IoT devices to monitor different employee's energy consumption patterns and calculate their carbon footprint. By equipping academic institutions with the necessary tools and data-driven insights, our study empowers them to effectively analyse emissions and implement targeted policies for reducing their carbon footprint.

articleTitle: Creative AI in Software Project Management
abstract: Software project management (SPM), which comprises planning, supervising, and keeping track of software projects, is a sophisticated art. However, the complexity and needs of modern software development projects are usually impossible for existing SPM methodologies to handle. The research paper investigates how business process reengineering (BPR) and the strategic application of artificial intelligence (AI) may enhance the effectiveness, quality, and competitiveness of software development processes. The development of artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to transform project management practices by automating operations, enabling project analytics, and offering intelligent recommendations. This paper proposes a framework for managing agile projects, which are gaining popularity due to their speedy value delivery and minimal risk of project failure. Just a few examples of how AI might be incorporated into project management include automating administrative tasks, providing data-driven risk predictions, simplifying project planning, and producing actionable insights. Software development is one of several businesses that has benefited from the popularity of Scrum and other agile project management methodologies. These methods are founded on a dynamic product backlog that consists of bug fixes and user stories. The specific issues that crop up when applying AI to project management are addressed using a five-step process. Using this method, which incorporates contextual considerations, problem-solution matching, and domainspecific implications, organizations can develop customized AI use cases.

articleTitle: Early-Stage Diabetes Risk Prediction Using Supervised Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: Diabetes is a common health problem worldwide; it is especially pervasive in Bangladesh. The condition manifests in a person when his blood sugar is consistently high. It also contributes to other health problems like blindness, renal failure, heart attack, and stroke. If you know about the early stage, you can take charge and maybe save someone's life. Sadly, this illness is spreading rapidly. The purpose of this research was to quantitatively evaluate the effectiveness of many widely used Machine Learning methods. The medical field is only one area that has benefited greatly from recent advancements in Machine Learning technology. Machine learning algorithms come in a wide variety. Nevertheless, in this research we employ five well-known machine learning algorithms to determine performance metrics: Gaussian Naive Bayes, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, and the Decision Tree classifier. Using real data from diabetic patients in Bangladesh, these algorithms were developed and evaluated. There are 3837 patient records in the dataset, 3057 of which correspond to affected cases and 396 were normal. Out of 5 different machine learning algorithms, Random Forest achieved the highest 98% accuracy.

articleTitle: Disaster Related Tweets Analysis with Machine Learning Approaches
abstract: It's no secret that the microblogging service Twitter (X) has quickly risen to prominence as one of the most reliable places to get the latest updates on breaking events. Tweets, Twitter's information streams, are sent out voluntarily by registered users and can reach even non-registered users, often before more conventional sources of mass news. In this research, we use machine learning to create models that can find helpful tweets on disasters automatically. Social media users provide massive amounts of data during natural catastrophe situations, some of which are useful for relief operations and emergency management. In this work, we analyze the material shared on social media during two hurricanes and one earthquake. This research has shown a machine-learning approach to categorizing tweets in relation to disasters and labeling Twitter data. This study has applied five machine learning algorithms to predict disaster and nondisaster tweets. In our model and among these five machine learning algorithms three perform similarly, but Logistic Regression has achieved the best 80.5% model accuracy among all other algorithms.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Framework for Industrial IoT Systems That Helps Preserve Privacy Using Poly1305 Encryption
abstract: This paper analyses how blockchain technology and smart contracts may be used to improve the safety and decentralization of Internet of Things (IoT) devices through the use of these two concepts. The two concepts under investigation are blockchain technology and smart contracts. This article presents a general overview of the problems that are caused by the insecurity of the internet of things (IoT), as well as the potential remedies that are based on blockchain technology. It examines the possibility that blockchain technology could make it possible for Internet of Things devices to have secure identity, data integrity, and privacy while at the same time offering decentralized control and consensus processes. In addition to this, the study evaluates the current state of blockchain-based Internet of Things solutions and makes a number of vital suggestions for future research directions with the intention of making such solutions even more effective. The overall focus of the paper is on the immense promise that blockchain technology and smart contracts have for addressing concerns about decentralisation and security in the Internet of Things (IoT), and it also provides a roadmap for future research in this area.

articleTitle: Predicting Song Likability: A Regression Approach Using User Demographics and Qualitative Feedback
abstract: In the contemporary digital music landscape, predicting song likability is of paramount importance for delivering personalized music experiences and advancing the music industry's recommendation systems. This paper introduces a novel approach that combines user demographics and qualitative feedback to enhance likability predictions. It has practical implications for personalized music recommendations and contributes to personalized recommendation system research. In contrast to conventional music recommendation systems that primarily rely on technical attributes and historical interactions, this approach unveils the profound relationship between personal characteristics and emotional bonds with music. Our study begins with a rigorous data collection and preprocessing phase, leveraging a comprehensive dataset from the Kaggle EMI Music Data Science Hackathon, cleaning, and exploratory analysis. Several regression algorithms were explored, with XGBoost Regression with K-Fold Cross Validation emerging as the top performer, offering accurate predictions. This research bridges the gap between listeners and music recommendation systems, improving music journeys.

articleTitle: Prediction of Heart Disease by Feature Selection Technique using Particle Swarm Optimization based on Logistic Regression
abstract: Heart disease is one of the main causes of illness and mortality in the modern world. in the world. Most of the deaths are occurring due to heart failure or some cardiovascular diseases. Therefore, it becomes crucial to identify abnormal heart behavior at an early stage. The prediction of disease at an early stage can lead to effective prevention and treatment. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for predicting heart disease by integrating feature selection techniques with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Logistic Regression (LR). A feature selection method based on PSO is used to increase prediction accuracy. PSO maximizes the predictive performance by reducing complexity to find the ideal combination of features for the feature subset iteratively will help the prediction model's performance. . Our results show that the proposed approach of using PSO to optimize the feature selection process of Logistic Regression for predicting heart disease is a promising idea that could increase the prediction of heart disease accuracy. The technique might enable medical practitioners to detect cardiac illness earlier and make better educated judgments that could result in earlier interventions and therapies that could save lives.

articleTitle: Lung Disease Classification Using Convolutional Neural Network (CNNs)
abstract: Lung and respiratory diseases claim millions of lives annually, and their treatment is hindered by the challenges in fast and accurate diagnosis. Access to specialized medical facilities for diagnosing and treating these conditions is limited globally. Even for those with access, the diagnostic process can be very expensive due to the cost of methods like CT or MRI scans, or the need for highly skilled radiologists when using cheaper alternatives such as x-rays. The demand for these professionals is high but the supply is extremely low as it takes several years of training for such a professional to be able to accurately diagnose conditions. The diagnostic process can also be time-consuming, ranging from half a day to several days. The primary goal of the paper is to maximize the benefits of costeffective x-ray diagnostic methods while leverage the capabilities of computer-aided diagnosis. This approach aims not only to reduce diagnosis time but also to minimize the risk of misdiagnosis. Additionally, it seeks to mitigate the shortage of radiologists in high-demand regions by augmenting their numbers and providing an alternative solution in areas lacking radiology expertise. To achieve these goals, a Web Application will be developed, serving as a diagnostic tool for lung and respiratory conditions. This application will provide an efficient, faster, affordable, and easily accessible means of diagnosing chest x-rays, aiding medical personnel in the detection and diagnosis of lung and respiratory diseases. This will speed up the diagnosis and will serve as a supplementary service for radiologists in areas lacking enough expertise.

articleTitle: Adaptive Harmonic Plus Noise Model (A-HNM) Analysis for Noise Reduction in Speech Signal
abstract: Speech signal enhancement has become a popular study area during the past few years. A plethora of techniques have been developed to improve the perceptibility and quality of speech signals. These techniques are frequently designed to restore the original signal from noise-damaged data. The wavelet transforms are commonly employed for processing speech signals. This research work proposes an Adaptive Harmonic plus Noise Model (A-HNM) analysis for removing the noise in speech signals. Initially, the speech signals from standard datasets are gathered and further, decomposed with the Empirical Mean Curve Decomposition (EMCD) technique. Then, the noise reduction is made over the decomposed signals with the help of A-HNM analysis, where the HNM parameters are tuned with the Red Deer Algorithm (RDA) to reduce the noise in the damaged speech signal and improve the performance. Additionally, the post-processing using wiener filtering is performed to increase the efficacy of standard improvement approaches.

articleTitle: Investigating the Power of Advanced Neural Network Architectures for Higher Quality Information Extraction
abstract: This paper explores the ability of superior neural community architectures to enhance the high quality of information extraction. It evaluates current architectures in the context of textual content report processing and examines how architectures can be changed to fit such responsibilities. The authors first speak about the capabilities of deep mastering frameworks for extracting data from text documents in terms of extracting semantic capabilities, categorizing records, and removing unique linguistic abilities. Then, they provide an in-depth overview of the diverse neural community architectures, including convolution and extended quick-term memory networks (LSTMs) and their packages for information extraction. Outcomes show that LSTMs are the most straightforward and efficient compared to other architectures, demonstrating accuracy, performance, and scalability benefits. The authors then discuss how current architectures, which include Caps Net and BERT, may be similarly optimized for information extraction responsibilities and recommend a technique for utilizing these strategies. In the end, the authors display how advanced neural community architectures may be used to extract better exceptional information from textual content documents, which has terrific ability implications for report processing, expertise extraction, and other duties.

articleTitle: Dangerous Farm Insects Detection Using Transfer Learning and CNN
abstract: In the ever-evolving landscape of machine learning, transfer learning has emerged as a powerful technique that leverages knowledge gained from one task to enhance the performance of another. This research paper delves into the realm of agricultural applications by employing the transfer learning technique on the “Dangerous Farm Insects Image Dataset.” This curated repository contains a diverse array of images depicting 15 distinct types of insects commonly found in agricultural environments, serving as a vital resource for understanding and studying these potentially destructive creatures. The focus of this study revolves around harnessing the pretrained knowledge of deep learning models and applying it to the task of classifying and identifying the various insect species within the dataset. By building upon the foundations laid by these models, we aim to optimize classification accuracy, reduce training time, and pave the way for real-world applications in pest management, crop protection, and beyond.

articleTitle: Predicting Bitcoin Prices for the Next 30 Days Using LSTM-Based Time Series Analysis
abstract: Particularly since Bitcoin's value and market capitalization have skyrocketed in recent years, the cryptocurrency market has attracted a lot of attention. For investors and traders, it is difficult to make wise selections due to the volatility and unpredictability of Bitcoin values. This project's goal is to forecast Bitcoin's price for the following 30 days. This prediction problem is particularly difficult due to the extreme price volatility of Bitcoin, the lack of conventional financial indications, and the complexity of the market. The price of Bitcoin for the following 30 days is predicted using a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network in this research. The model is trained using a dataset of historical Bitcoin prices and their corresponding features such as trading volume and market capitalization. The LSTM model is trained to capture the temporal dependencies and patterns in the data, which allows it to make predictions. Previous studies have used various machine learning algorithms to predict Bitcoin prices, including ARIMA, SVM, and Random Forest. However, LSTM has shown superior performance in capturing the temporal dependencies in sequential data. The proposed LSTM model was evaluated using metrics such as Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and the results showed that the LSTM model outperforms the previous studies' models in terms of accuracy. The proposed model's predictions can assist investors and traders in making informed decisions about buying or selling Bitcoin in the future.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Biomedical and Health Informatics: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence for Improved Healthcare Solutions
abstract: This paper explores the convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) with Biomedical and Health Informatics, focusing on the transformative potential of AI-driven solutions in the healthcare domain. With the growing availability of healthcare data and advancements in AI technologies, there is an increasing emphasis on leveraging AI techniques to enhance medical diag- nosis, treatment, and patient care. This paper highlights recent research and applications that demonstrate the impact of AI in areas such as medical image analysis, disease prediction, drug discovery, and personalized medicine. Additionally, it addresses the challenges and ethical considerations associated with integrating AI into healthcare systems, emphasizing the need for robust and interpretable AI models, data privacy, and trustworthiness. By delving into the opportunities and challenges presented by AI in Biomedical and Health Informatics, this paper aims to inspire further research and collaboration in this promising and critical intersection of disciplines.

articleTitle: Prediction of Probability of Server Intrusion Using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: This research paper offers a comprehensive examination of the phenomenon of hostile server incursions in the field of cybersecurity. Given the increasing frequency and complexity of cyber threats, it is crucial to comprehend the subtleties of these assaults in order to design effective responses. This paper investigates several forms of malevolent server breaches, examining their methodology and probable ramifications. Considerable importance is attributed to the identification of new patterns and developing attack routes, hence illuminating the dynamic characteristics inherent in cyber threats. Furthermore, the present study puts forward a set of complete countermeasures, using state-of-the-art technology and strategic methodologies, with the aim of strengthening server defenses. Through the integration of empirical data and the use of sophisticated analytical methods, our study endeavors to provide significant contributions in terms of meaningful insights for professionals in the field of cybersecurity, policymakers, and fellow researchers. This study aims to improve the robustness of servers and minimize the consequences of hostile incursions in the rapidly growing digital environment, which is seeing a rise in attacks on digital assets.

articleTitle: Investigation of Endorsement Guideline Protocol Actuality Problem Using Blowfish AES Algorithm
abstract: A larger an organization's dependence on, Potential distributed information systems for its everyday activities, the greater its vulnerability to security vulnerabilities, even as it gains efficiency and productivity advantages. These approaches for massive data must include a method for imposing a policy regarding the content, topic, credentials, and type of data being produced. Organizations that used FPT (Fixed Parameter Tractable) for transmitting client information experienced issues such as the following: Loss of data, transmission file restriction, unauthorized access to data, and confidentiality are all concerns. The data security area is confronted with several new challenges. Variables such as the evaluation of security issues and the decentralization of access to the information are taken into consideration. The proposed Blowfish AES algorithm is used to secure the data to overcome these issues. The Blowfish AES algorithm, which consists of encryption and decryption, makes use of a key to allow the receiver to unwrap the message. An individual can only access the data if all their qualifications have been verified and accepted by the system. The samples are the most important part of them because they are computation time destructive and have exactness problems. The authenticated people could indeed access the information to complete the task, and an acknowledgement is sent to the authenticated person.

articleTitle: Innovative Low-Cost Field Protection (LCFP) Technique: Safeguarding Agricultural Land and Crops through Advanced Technology Integration
abstract: Precision agriculture, characterized by integrating cutting-edge technologies to optimize farming practices, has opened up new possibilities for modern agricultural management. The present study introduces an innovative solution, Low-Cost Field Protection (LCFP) technique, meticulously tailored to safeguard agricultural land and crops from persistent threats posed by different creatures. This cutting-edge approach integrates advanced technologies to optimize farming practices and enhance precision agriculture. The LCFP technique employs a comprehensive and highly efficient three-module design to identify and repel potential intruders with remarkable efficacy. The first module uses a Passive Infrared (PIR) sensor and an image sensor to detect animals, capturing images for further analysis. The system leverages the state-of-the-art object detection algorithm YOLOv5 and the widely acclaimed COCO dataset for precise animal recognition in the second module. Finally, the third module, driven by a Raspberry Pi, sends data about the detected animals and triggers ultrasound frequencies to sound an alarm through a buzzer, effectively deterring threats. With cost-effectiveness- at its core, the LCFP promises substantial mitigation of crop damages, elevating overall agricultural productivity, and advancing sustainability. By providing farmers with a vital proactive tool to respond swiftly to threats, the LCFP is a practical and reliable solution for protecting crops and agricultural land from various animal and bird attacks.

articleTitle: Comparing and Contrasting Automated Reasoning Techniques in Comparative Information Analysis
abstract: This technical abstract discusses the software program of various automated reasoning techniques for comparative statistics evaluation. Automatic reasoning uses hard and fast predetermined algorithms to analyze a given set of information. Within comparative statistics analysis, such algorithms may be used to find similarities, versions, and patterns among numerous information sets. The distinct varieties of automated reasoning strategies for comparative statistics analysis are rule-based reasoning, feature optimization, regression analysis, gadget learning, and Bayesian techniques. For every one of those techniques, the paper will communicate how they provide precise blessings for comparative statistics evaluation and how they'll be achieved in beautiful datasets. Furthermore, it'll evaluate and assess the benefits and shortcomings of each of those techniques. This technical abstract offers a top-level view of the capabilities and annoying conditions of the diverse automatic reasoning strategies applicable to comparative statistics evaluation.

articleTitle: IoT-Driven Holistic Sleep Aid System
abstract: Sleep is a vital part of human health and an essential part of our daily lives. Sleep aids provide a range of solutions for people with sleep problems. This research study presents a holistic sleep aid system in response to the many issues that sleep disorders present. The Sleep Aid System uses the Internet of Things (IoT) to remotely access and monitor vital sleep-related data, such as body temperature. The system utilizes the power of the ATmega328P microcontroller to orchestrate precise environmental adjustments. Integrating the NodeMCU with an ESP8266 chip significantly extends the system's capabilities, allowing for remote monitoring and control. In addition, a strategically placed Passive Infrared (PIR) sensor enhances sleep quality by detecting motion during sleep cycles. This thoughtfully crafted hardware configuration forms the foundation of the Sleep Aid system, granting users precise control over their sleep environment while enabling comprehensive sleep monitoring. In conclusion, our research study demonstrates the possibilities of hardware-driven approaches for dealing with one of the cornerstones of human well-being: sound, peaceful sleep.

articleTitle: Mapping AI-Driven Marketing: Review of Field and Directions for Future Research
abstract: Businesses increasingly function more effectively as a result of disruptive technologies like the IoT, AI, BDA, and Blockchain. Artificial Intelligence (AI), which has the biggest potential to change marketing, is the most current disruptive technology. The top AI solutions for marketing functions are being sought after by international practitioners. However, a thorough analysis of the literature can show how useful artificial intelligence (AI) is for marketing while also outlining potential research areas. The current study provides a comprehensive assessment of AI in marketing using bibliometric, conceptual, intellectual network, and thematic map analysis of the available literature published between 2014 and 2023. Bibliometric analysis was done through Biblioshiny using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> and Vos viewer software. A thorough analysis of three hundred fifty-six publications allowed for the identification of the scientific actors that performed the best. Furthermore, cocitation analysis offered the intellectual and conceptual framework.

articleTitle: Routing attack Detection using Ensemble Artificial Intelligence Model for IIoT
abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has risen dramatically and blocked practically all requests due to the fast growth and expansion of brainy schemes and independent, energy-aware sensing plans. IIoT-based botnet assaults have increased, despite the limits of IIoT devices in terms of compute, storage, and connectivity. A scheme that can create profiles for malicious events via IoT networks is required to counteract this threat. To detect botnet attacks in IIoT networks, we offer a machine learning ensemble model that analyses IoT network behaviour characteristics and using ensemble learning to spot out-of-the-ordinary traffic caused by compromised IoT nodes. We also compare four distinct machine learning methods, including Generalized Additive Models (GAMs), Random Forests (RF), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and XGBoost, to define our IoT-based botnet detection strategy. We utilised the dataset, which includes logs of both benign IoT attack IIoT devices, to assess the quality of the projected model. The testing findings show that our optional model has a high detection accuracy of 96.42 percent against botnet assaults initiated from hacked IIoT devices. We also compare the proposed model's ensemble findings to those of existing state-of-the-art methods, showing that they are superior.

articleTitle: Enhancing Modern Power System Resilience with Superconducting Fault Current Limiters
abstract: The contemporary electrical power grid confronts a growing need for effective and dependable electricity distribution. However, as this progress continues, it ushers in fresh challenges, particularly in the management of fault currents, which can result in equipment damage, grid instability, and power interruptions. In response to these critical issues, the integration of Superconducting Fault Current Limiters (SFCLs) has emerged as a focal point in modern power system discussions. SFCLs harness the distinctive properties of superconducting materials to efficiently mitigate fault currents, all while upholding the stability of the grid. This article offers a comprehensive abstract that explores the application of SFCLs as a protective mechanism for contemporary power systems. The abstract commences by elucidating the mounting necessity for mitigating fault currents, driven by the proliferation of sensitive electronic equipment, the adoption of renewable energy sources, and the expansion of distributed generation. It proceeds to introduce the foundational principles of superconductivity and its practical utilization in limiting fault currents. To validate the proposed methodologies, an enhanced IEEE33 bus test system is employed, and all simulations are conducted within the MATLAB Simulink environment. This research seeks to address the pressing concerns surrounding fault current management in modern power systems, presenting a multifaceted approach that combines theoretical foundations with practical solutions.

articleTitle: Multi-Class Text Classification using Machine Learning & Deep Learning
abstract: Text classification indeed holds a central position in the field of natural language processing (NLP) and has a wide range of applications across diverse domains. In this paper, we investigate the effectiveness of BERT & DistilBERT embeddings in combination with long short-term memory (LSTM), convolutional neural networks (CNN), and bi-directional LSTM (bi-LSTM) architectures for text classification on the widely recognized 20 Newsgroups dataset. We propose an approach that utilizes BERT & DistilBERT embeddings to capture contextual information and feed it into the CNN, LSTM, and bi-LSTM models. This combination enables the models to effectively learn hierarchical representations and capture both local and global dependencies in the text data. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed CNN, LSTM, and bi-LSTM models outperform Siamese networks, which have previously been explored for text classification on the 20 Newsgroups dataset. Our models consistently demonstrate superior accuracy and deliver enhanced performance in terms of precision, recall, and F1-score across diverse classes. Our proposed models not only outperform Siamese networks but also provide insights into the importance of leveraging contextual embeddings for more accurate and robust text classification. A maximum accuracy of 92.94% was achieved when using distil-BERT with bi-LSTM and a minimum of 87.76% when using LSTM.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Deep Neural Network Technique for Prediction of Morality Risk in Patients with Corona Virus Disease
abstract: Predicting risks in patients with Corona Virus Disease 19 (COVID-19) involves assessing the likelihood and severity of various outcomes, such as hospitalization, ICU admission, disease progression, or mortality. Machine learning models, including deep neural networks, can be used for this task by leveraging patient data to make predictions. In contrast to using deep learning techniques for COVID-19 disease detection through image analysis, an approach was proposed that combined feature selection, instance clustering and Deep Neural Network (DNN) to forecast the threat of morality in COVID-19 patients. However, DNN struggles with handling uncertain and imprecise data. In addition to this, DNN is sensitive to variations and outliers in the input data. In this paper, Fuzzy DNN (FDNN) is introduced to handle the uncertainty, data variation and outliers in input data for better prediction of risks in patients with COVID-19. FDNN is a deep neural network that combines fuzzy and neural representations to derive information. The knowledge obtained from both views is integrated to create the final data representation for prediction of risks in patients with COID-19. The findings indicate that the suggested approach using FDNN yields superior accuracy, precision, and recall in predicting COVID19 patients.

articleTitle: The Classification of Breast Cancer Using a Transfer Learning Strategy in a Federated Learning Framework
abstract: In order to make an accurate forecast, deep learning algorithms need a sizable quantity of data to learn from. Recent research has shown that transfer learning-based DL techniques to developing CAD systems function properly across a range of use cases. Diseases including lung cancer, brain tumours, and breast cancer are detected and analysed at an early stage by employing these systems and their many modalities. Pre-trained models are often used for DL-based activities in computer vision instead of creating models of neural networks from scratch. This article explains why transfer learning models may be used to automate tumour classification without the need for augmentation or preprocessing. On the BreakHis dataset, seven machine learning models are used for tumour classification; Xception achieved the highest accuracy (83.07<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) among these seven models. DarkN et53 also excels in computing a new measure called Balanced Accuracy (BAC) (87.17%), which is necessary for achieving accuracy with an imbalanced dataset. This discovery will help scientists and doctors choose the best model for tumour classification when faced with an imbalanced data set. It will help doctors categorise the illness more accurately and quickly.

articleTitle: Security Challenges for Topology Maintenance of MANET by Trust Evaluation Mechanism
abstract: Protecting the security, privacy, and accessibility of an NIDS, or Network Intrusion Detection System, is a must. Among the various commercial applications of machine learning methods, deep learning stands out as the most significant. An efficient machine learning-based intrusion detection system is necessary for dealing with hostile activity in networks. In this study, we offer a PCA- and Residual Network-based intrusion detection system that is both quick and reliable. Dimensionality reduction is achieved by using PCA. We next create a ResNet and investigate how changing the number of primary components <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(k)$</tex> and the time-related parameter size (time-step t) affects ResNet's classification accuracy (CA) on the UNSW_NBI5 dataset. We present a quick optimization approach for choosing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex>. Based on experimental results, our strategy achieves over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$98{{\%}}$</tex> accuracy in binary-classification with a rate of false alarms of less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.8{{\%}}$</tex> and a duration of fewer than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$400{\mathrm{s}}$</tex> in the training time. The accuracy for many classes is over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$86{{\%}}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Current State of Document Ingestion and Understanding
abstract: This paper addresses the need to convert unstructured data, like documents and images, into structured formats to enhance accessibility and usability. It discusses various subtasks, such as document extraction, text summarization, and image identification, highlighting their significance in improving data understanding and accessibility. These tasks have practical applications in fields like medicine, education, information retrieval and decision-making. Overall, this paper explores the importance of structured data in our data-driven world. Exploration of such tasks in document ingestion and understanding sheds light on the technology available yet not used in a manner to ease the understanding and availability of documents to a commoner.
